class ActuatorBase

Bases: ComponentBase

Base class for robot actuators.

Mirrors ControllerBase and SensorBase: derives from ComponentBase for common lifecycle (validity, actor, destroy). No concrete actuators exist yet; this establishes the contract early so the first actuator follows the same shape as controllers and sensors.

Registration contract (a RoboticsContext::RegisterActuator<T> template lands with the first concrete actuator, mirroring RegisterController/RegisterSensor): every actuator must declare static constexpr std::string_view TypeName() { return “…”; } (used by the registration templates and for the generated Python type_name() binding), implement std::string_view GetTypeName() const override; // returns TypeName() and provide a uniform constructor ActuatorX(Actor* actor, std::string_view paramArgs, Error& error); that loads its own params from the path or inline JSON. An (Actor*, Params const&, Error&) overload is recommended for programmatic / non-filesystem construction.

Teardown contract (mirrors ControllerBase / SensorBase): get_actor() resolves the live actor on demand and yields None once the owning mochi Scene (or the actor) is gone, so an actuator that outlives its Scene (Scene destroyed before the RoboticsContext) sees get_actor() == None in its destructor. Any concrete actuator whose destructor releases actor-held resources must therefore guard on GetActor() != None (or, for context-owned resources, resolve via GetContext()) so teardown never dereferences a dangling Actor*.

class BaseSceneParams(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: object

Scene definition within a .superdex_scene.

The base_scene is optional — a scene under construction may not have one yet. When present it is the authoritative source for all simulation physics parameters (gravity, solver config, contact filtering, collision layers, etc.); when absent the scene keeps its default parameters.

property base_scene

Path to a .mochi_scene file. Defines the scene foundation. Empty means no base scene.

property spawnable_prefabs

Prefabs that can be loaded/destroyed on demand at runtime (e.g. task objects spawned each episode).

property task_root

Where this scene’s task frame (the nominal table top) is in the world. Every task’s root-level spawns are placed onto it, through the task’s taskRootOffset when it declares one. Unset leaves every task where its own coordinates put it.

class Bot

Bases: object

Runtime interface to a bot instance in a Scene.

A Bot wraps a single articulated Actor with the controllers, sensors, and actuators created for it. Bots are created via create_bot() and destroyed via destroy_bot(). The RoboticsContext owns the bot memory allocated and deallocated by these functions, respectively. The raw Bot* returned by create_bot() remains valid until destroy_bot() is called or the RoboticsContext is destroyed.

Note

Not thread-safe – like the underlying Scene, a Bot must only be accessed from the thread that owns its scene (usually in an async callback if using async scenes.)

create_actuator

Create an actuator of the given type on one of this bot’s links. The actuator counterpart to create_sensor(), for actuators only known at runtime rather than declared as a BotActuatorPrefab. It joins get_actuator_handles() and is destroyed with the bot.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered actuator type.

  • link_name (str) – Name of the link (from links) to attach the actuator to.

  • name (str) – Instance name, used by find_actuators_by_name(). Names need not be unique.

  • param_args (str) – Optional params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

Returns:

Pointer to the new actuator, or None on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

get_controller

Resolve a controller handle to its underlying ControllerBase.

Unlike get_controller(), which resolves any handle in the context, this checks the controller belongs to this bot first — so a handle from another bot, or from a standalone actor, is reported as an error rather than silently resolved.

Parameters:

controller_handle (ControllerHandle) – Handle returned by get_controller_handles().

Returns:

Pointer to the controller, or None on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

get_controller_handles

Get the handles of every controller this bot owns.

Covers controllers created through create_controller() and those created on one of this bot’s actors with create_controller() — the owning bot is inferred from the actor (see get_bot_containing_actor()), so how a controller was created makes no difference to whether it appears here. Mirrors get_sensor_handles(): the same set the bot-scoped finders draw from, and the same set destroy_bot() tears down. Resolve each handle with get_controller().

Returns:

A snapshot of the bot’s controller handles, in creation order.

get_sensor_handles

Get the handles of every sensor this bot owns.

Covers sensors declared per link in the BotPrefab via BotSensorPrefab and instantiated by create_bot(), those added afterwards via create_sensor(), and those created straight off one of this bot’s actors with create_sensor() — the owning bot is inferred from the actor (see get_bot_containing_actor()), so how a sensor was created makes no difference to whether it appears here. This is the same set the bot-scoped finders draw from, and the same set destroy_bot() tears down. Use get_sensor() on each handle to obtain the underlying SensorBase pointer.

Returns:

the links entries first (by link, then by per-link sensor index), followed by any later additions.

Return type:

A snapshot of the bot’s sensor handles in creation order

class BotContactOverride(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: object

Used to explicitly enable or disable contact between links in a bot. By default, all bots will spawn with contact disabled between links and their first ancestor with a physics body not connected via a Hard joint. This structure can be used to either reenable contact on those pairs, or disable contact between links that are not strictly child-parent. Overrides are applied on bot link actors after spawn using enable_actor_contact_symmetric().

See also

contact_overrides, enable_actor_contact_symmetric()

property enable

Should contact between the pair be enabled?

property link_a

The first link in the pair.

property link_b

The second link in the pair.

class BotJointPrefab(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: ArticulatedJointPrefab

Parameters describing a single joint in a bot.

property effort_limit

Maximum effort magnitude that may be applied to actuate this joint [N·m for revolute, N for prismatic]. Interpreted by regime: a negative value (default EFFORT_UNBOUNDED) is unbounded; 0 is non-actuated (no effort can be applied, though the joint still moves freely within its range under external forces); a positive value is a finite limit. This is advisory metadata — it is not copied into the physics articulation, so the sim enforces nothing on its own; controllers may read it (e.g. to clamp their output).

class BotLinearTransmissionPrefab(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: BotTransmissionPrefab

Parameters describing a single linear transmission attached to a bot.

Mirrors superdex::experimental::LinearTransmissionParams with an added display name field and SReflect markup so it can live inside BotPrefab and round-trip through the bot’s JSON serialization. The three joint arrays (joint_indices, joint_coefficients, joint_axis_disps) must always be the same length, with one entry per joint the transmission traverses. The remaining fields are inherited from BotTransmissionPrefab which inherits superdex::experimental::DisplacementControlActuatorParams so that one displacement-control actuator can be configured alongside each transmission.

property joint_axis_disps

Displacement along the joint axis [m] for the transmission attachment point at each joint. This allows the transmission to be offset from the joint origin along the axis.

property joint_coefficients

Transmission Jacobian entry at each joint [m / joint-DoF units for a tendon, dimensionless for a gearbox]. Sign encodes direction: positive if the transmission displacement increases with the joint DoF, negative if it decreases.

property joint_indices

Indices into joints identifying which joints the transmission traverses.

class BotPrefab(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: object

Complete parameter set for a bot.

property contact_overrides

Array of link-link contact override pairs.

property cycles

Cycle-closing joints for closed-loop mechanisms (e.g. four-bar linkages, parallel grippers). Each entry becomes one superdex::ArticulatedActorParams::cycles entry at instantiation time. Link references (superdex::ArticulatedCycleJointParams::parentLink / superdex::ArticulatedCycleJointParams::childLink) are int indices into links.

property default_pose

Default pose (array of joint DOF angles/translations) used when spawning the bot.

property joints

Joint parameters for each joint in the articulation.

property linear_transmissions

Linear transmissions that couple multiple joint DOFs via per-joint coefficients. Each entry produces one superdex::experimental::LinearTransmissionParams at instantiation time.

property links

Link parameters for each link in the articulation.

property name

Bot name.

property scale

[Experimental] Uniform scale applied when the bot is instantiated. Meant for sizing human hand bots to a tracked hand (XR teleoperation), not for robots. The asset stays in nominal units; the created actor’s geometry, shapes, skin, sensor offsets, prismatic limits and default pose are scaled, masses by scale^3 and rotational inertias by scale^5, and joint friction, inertia, limit stiffness and damping and cycle stiffness for dynamic similarity. Rotational limits are unchanged. Contact parameters are not scaled. Spawn poses, controller gains and prefab-space utilities are nominal; effort limits and anything read from or sent to the live actor, such as pose-controller targets, are in scaled units. Must be positive and finite; values other than 1 are rejected for bots with linear transmissions or spatial tendons, and for bots composed with mods.

property skin

Optional deformable skin skinned over the articulation’s links, acting as a contact collidee. When present, produces the superdex::ArticulatedActorParams::skin at instantiation time.

property spatial_tendons

Spatial tendons routed through waypoint and linear-joint elements. Each entry produces one superdex::experimental::SpatialTendonParams at instantiation time.

property world_from_root

Transform from the root link to the world frame.

Overloaded function.

  1. spawn_prefab_instance(self, instance_name: str, prefab_name: str, world_from_instance: superdex.physics.TransformRT) -> Span[superdex.physics.ActorHandle]

Spawn a spawnable prefab under an instance name at a world pose.

Instances are keyed by instance name, not prefab name, so the same prefab may be spawned any number of times. The instance name prefixes the created actor names, and is the identity the rest of the pipeline keys off (the recorded HDF5 object id and the dataset/replay feature key; see name). The instance does not replace the scene’s gravity or solver settings. A .superdex_bot / .superdex_bot_archive spawnable is instantiated as an articulated Bot named after the instance and rooted at worldFromInstance; the instance owns it.

Parameters:

  • instance_name (str) – Unique, non-empty instance name; must not already be live.

  • prefab_name (str) – Spawnable-prefab name declared in this scene.

  • world_from_instance (TransformRT) – Instance root pose in world space.

Returns:

Actor handles in prefab AddToScene order (for a bot, its articulated actor), or empty on error. Valid until the instance is destroyed.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

  1. spawn_prefab_instance(self, instance_name: str, prefab_name: str, world_from_instance: superdex.physics.TransformRT, edit: str) -> Span[superdex.physics.ActorHandle]

Like the overload above, with an edit set in the prefab before its shapes load, e.g. to rebuild a recorded spawn.

An empty edit changes nothing; one that does not fit the prefab spawns nothing.

Parameters:

  • edit (str) – The fields to set in the prefab, as a JSON object (DiffPrefab writes one).

Returns:

Actor handles in prefab AddToScene order, or empty on error. Valid until the instance is destroyed.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

class ComponentBase

Bases: object

Base class for all bots components (controllers, sensors, actuators). Provides common state: the associated actor’s stale-safe identity, a validity flag, and the Destroy pattern. The validity flag is set to false by RoboticsContext before deletion, allowing dangling-pointer detection alongside generational handles.

The associated actor is NOT cached as a raw pointer. Its stale-safe identity (ActorHandle / SceneHandle / owning Mochi context) is retained and get_actor() resolves the live Actor* on demand, yielding None once the owning scene (or the actor) has been destroyed. A component that outlives its mochi Scene (e.g. the Scene was destroyed before the RoboticsContext) therefore never dereferences a dangling Actor* — callers check get_actor() for None. This assumes the mochi Mochi context outlives the RoboticsContext — the outermost lifetime in the mochi ownership graph.

get_actor

Resolve the live Actor* this component is bound to, or None if it was constructed without an actor or its owning scene/actor has since been destroyed. Resolved on demand from the stale-safe handle each call (an O(1) scene lookup), so it is always current and never returns a dangling pointer — dereference only after a None check.

Returns:

Live associated actor, or None if none is available.

get_name

This component’s instance name, or empty if it was created without one. Names are NOT required to be unique, so name-based lookups (FindByName) may return multiple matches.

Returns:

Instance name; empty if unnamed.

get_owning_bot

The bot this component was created on, or None if it was created directly on an actor (not via a bot) — e.g. a scene-level sensor or a controller built on a raw articulation. Used to scope FindByName / FindByType to a single bot and to drive DestroyBot’s component cascade. Borrowed: the owning bot is owned by the RoboticsContext, which destroys a bot’s components before the bot itself, so this never dangles. Held as a raw pointer (not a handle) because a bot is not scene-owned, so the stale-safety the actor handles provide is unnecessary here.

Returns:

Owning bot, or None if this component has no owning bot.

get_type_name

This component’s registered type name (e.g. “BASIC_OSC_PD”, “SENSOR_CAMERA”), reported polymorphically. Declared here so controllers, sensors, and actuators can be searched by type uniformly (FindByType); each component kind implements it.

Returns:

Registered component type name.

is_valid

Whether this component remains usable. Returns false after its owning RoboticsContext destroys it.

Returns:

True while the component is live.

reset

Reset internal state without destroying the component. Parameters are preserved. Use between episodes to clear stale state (e.g., derivative tracking, timing diagnostics).

class ControllerBasicOscPd

Bases: ControllerBase

Basic operational-space PD (impedance) controller for robotic arms.

Computes joint torques via the Jacobian transpose method: tau = J^T * F, where F = Kp * pose_error + Kd * velocity_error combines position/rotation tracking errors with PD gains. This is the minimal, robot-agnostic core of operational-space control:

  • No nullspace or posture bias. Redundant (extra-DOF) arms are free to drift in the nullspace; only the end-effector pose is regulated.

  • Per-DOF effort clamping (direction-preserving vector scaling), enabled by default; the per-joint effort limits are harvested from the controller’s BotPrefab (see Initialize).

  • No joint/velocity-limit avoidance, friction/gravity compensation, or inertia decoupling; those belong to richer controllers (see the internal OSC variants).

Intended as a clean, open-sourceable baseline that works on any articulated arm without robot-specific tuning tables.

  • target (ControllerBasicOscPdTarget) – Target setpoint.

Returns:

Efforts for all DOFs [Nm]. Uncontrolled DOFs are set to 0. Empty span on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Basic operational-space PD controller parameters.

Minimal parameter set for a robot-agnostic task-space impedance controller. See ControllerBasicOscPd for details.

property b_apply_max_error_magnitude_normalization

If true, renormalize the task-space error so translation and rotation errors stay below their configured maximums, keeping the force direction consistent. Requires positive maxTranslationError and maxRotationError.

property b_apply_max_osc_torque_normalization

If true, scale the output efforts down uniformly so that no controlled DOF exceeds the per-joint effort limit harvested from the controller’s BotPrefab (see Initialize), preserving the task-space force direction. Requires the controller to have been constructed with a BotPrefab; only joints with a finite (positive) effortLimit constrain the scaling — unbounded (negative) and non-actuated (zero) joints are ignored.

class ControllerEntry(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: object

A controller instance to create and attach to a bot.

property init_args

The controller’s init args as a serialized JSON object – the contents of the scene entry’s nested “initArgs” object (e.g. {“baseLinkName”:..,”eeLinkName”:..} for link-resolved controllers, or a model path for a learned controller). Passed verbatim to ControllerBase::ConfigureFromSceneEntry, which deserializes it into a controller-specific struct, so the scene loader never needs to know a controller’s fields. Reflected with the JsonString attribute: on load the nested “initArgs” object is captured into this string, and on save it is re-emitted as a nested object (round-trip identity), so no bespoke parsing is needed. May also be set or modified directly (e.g. from Python) before LoadBotScene. Defaults to an empty object (“{}”), which NoSerializeDefaults omits from the saved file. (Legacy scenes that interleave flat controller fields instead of a nested “initArgs” object are folded into this string at load time – see LoadBotScenePrefabFromFile; new scenes and all saves use the nested form.)

property name

Instance name for runtime lookup.

property params

Controller-specific parameters as a raw JSON string. Omit to use defaults.

property type

Controller type identifier (registered string), e.g. “BASIC_OSC_PD”, “BASIC_JSC_PD”.

class RoboticsContext

Bases: object

Resource owner for bots, controllers, sensors, and actuators.

Owns the memory for bots, controllers, sensors, and actuators created through it.

create_actuator

Create an actuator of the given type on the given link actor. Unlike a sensor, an actuator always drives a body, so linkActor is required: passing None sets an error and returns an invalid handle. paramArgs is an optional params file path or inline JSON string; empty uses default-constructed parameters. name is the instance name used by find_actuators_by_name() and need not be unique. The owning bot is inferred from linkActor. Returns a handle. For bot-owned actuators, prefer declaring them in the BotPrefab so they are auto-instantiated and destroyed with the bot.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered actuator type name.

  • link_actor (Actor) – Actor the actuator drives; must not be None.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

  • param_args (str) – Params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

Returns:

Handle to the created actuator, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

create_controller

Create a controller of the given type for robot. Harvests model-derived configuration (e.g. per-joint effort limits) from the optional borrowed prefab: pass None to create on a raw articulated actor with no model (the prefab must outlive the controller otherwise).

robot may also be None, to drive a real robot with observations pushed in from outside instead of read off a Mochi articulation. Anything that needs the articulation (e.g. reading a Jacobian) then has to be supplied externally, and the controller reports an error if asked for it. A controller that cannot work at all without a simulation rejects the None actor itself — see ControllerMochiArticulatedPose, which drives Mochi’s built-in implicit PD controller.

The owning bot is inferred from robot (see get_bot_containing_actor()): if that actor is a bot’s articulation or one of its link actors, the controller is recorded against that bot, found by the bot-scoped finders, and destroyed with it; otherwise it has no owning bot. create_controller() is the more direct way to create one on a bot you already hold, and also carries an instance name.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered controller type name.

  • prefab (Optional[BotPrefab]) – Optional borrowed robot-model description; may be None and must outlive the created controller.

  • robot (Optional[Actor]) – Articulated actor to control, or None for externally supplied observations.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

Returns:

Handle to the created controller, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

create_sensor

Create a sensor of the given type on the given link actor. paramArgs is an optional params file path or inline JSON string consumed by the factory; pass an empty view to use default-constructed parameters. name is the instance name used by find_sensors_by_name() and need not be unique. The owning bot is inferred from linkActor. Returns a handle. For bot-owned sensors, prefer declaring them in the BotPrefab so they are auto-instantiated and destroyed with the bot.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered sensor type name.

  • link_actor (Optional[Actor]) – Actor to attach the sensor to, or None for an actor-less sensor.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

  • param_args (str) – Params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

Returns:

Handle to the created sensor, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

find_bots_by_name

Find all bots whose name (from name) equals name. Bot names are not unique (multiple bots may share a prefab name), so any number of handles may be returned (empty if none). There is no FindBotsByType: a bot has no registered type.

get_bot_containing_actor

Find the bot containing actor. Accepts either a bot’s articulation actor or any of its link actors. Returns None when the actor is contained by no bot, which is a valid result: a scene may hold standalone actors and articulations from plain mochi prefabs alongside its bots. A None actor also returns None.

class SpawnEntry(*args, **kwargs)

Bases: object

A single named object instance to spawn on top of a .superdex_scene.

Declares which spawnable prefab to instantiate (by name) and where. The instance name is the key used everywhere downstream — it becomes the recorded object id (HDF5 group), the dataset/replay feature key, and the Unreal actor label — so a task can spawn multiple instances of the same prefab_name under distinct names.

property name

Unique instance name within the task (e.g. “Foam2”, “m8_knob”).

property parent

Name of another spawn entry whose transform this spawn is relative to, or the reserved literal “task_root” (also the implicit default when empty) to place this spawn in the task actor’s own frame. parent_from_spawn, and any PoseRandomization offset, are interpreted in the parent’s local frame; the parent’s resolved (post-DR) world transform is composed in after randomization. Parent chains may be arbitrarily deep. Cycles and references to undefined spawn names are rejected by ValidateBotTaskPrefab.

property parent_from_spawn

Local pose relative to parent (aFromB convention: maps spawn-frame coordinates into the parent frame). Default: identity.

property prefab_name

Name of a spawnable prefab declared in the .superdex_scene’s scene.spawnablePrefabs[]. Multiple spawns may reference the same prefab.

apply_asset_snapshot(snapshot: AssetSnapshot, asset_root: str) → str

Pin every file in a snapshot for the rest of the process, so each loads from its version instead, replacing any snapshot already applied.

Entries are resolved against assetRoot, the directory holding the scene’s .superdex_root, wherever its asset tree is mounted. Every version must exist, beside the file it pins, and no version may itself be a pinned file. Then load the scene from the returned path as usual: the scene and every file it references, however deeply, load from their pinned versions. A file under assetRoot, or under the .superdex_root directory of any pinned file, that the snapshot does not pin fails to load instead of loading its tip. Applying fails if a pinned .superdex_root no longer matches its version. Loaded assets carry the versions’ paths, so don’t save assets while a snapshot is applied; archiving is refused. Call clear_asset_snapshot() to stop applying it. On failure no snapshot is applied, including any applied before.

Parameters:

  • snapshot (AssetSnapshot) – The snapshot to apply.

  • asset_root (str) – Directory containing the .superdex_root the snapshot’s paths are relative to.

Returns:

Absolute path of the snapshot’s scene, to load as usual.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

build_articulated_pose_from_bot_pose(bot_prefab: BotPrefab, src_pose: Span[float], num_actor_dofs: int) → superdex.physics.DynamicArrayReal

Convert a bot-space pose to an articulated-actor pose.

Bot DOFs never include the root joint’s, whether or not the articulation has any: a Free root contributes 6 actor DOFs that bot space excludes, and a Hard root contributes none. The two spaces therefore share an order and differ only by that leading offset, so this copies srcPose to pose[i + numBaseDofs] and zero-fills the base DOFs, producing the actor-DOF layout set_articulated_pose_from_joints() expects. It never permutes.

Parameters:

  • bot_prefab (BotPrefab) – Bot describing the articulation.

Create a Bot runtime object from a BotPrefab. Builds the underlying articulated actor in scene and seeds its default pose. The returned Bot owns no scene resources beyond the actor — destroy it with destroy_bot(). This must be in the scene thread (i.e. in an async callback if using async scenes.)

Returns:

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

create_context() → RoboticsContext

derive(seed: int, key: str, index: int | None = ...) → int

Deterministic 64-bit sub-seed from a master seed and a stable key.

Stateless and order-independent. Returns a seed for the caller’s random generator; it does not sample values. Uses the FNV-1a key hash XOR seed, SplitMix64-finalized. Parity-locked to the Python DR derivation: both must match bit-for-bit, and the C++ and Python golden-vector sets must stay in sync. The golden vectors in test/derive_test.cpp define the seed contract. Different keys can collide; this is not a cryptographic hash.

Parameters:

  • seed (int) – Master seed.

  • key (str) – Stable string key, hashed as UTF-8 bytes.

  • index (Optional[int]) – Optional index; None and 0 are distinct.

Returns:

Deterministic 64-bit sub-seed in [0, 2^64).

Parameters:

  • bot (Optional[Bot]) – Pointer to the bot to be destroyed.

Load bot parameters from an MJCF (MuJoCo XML) file.

Bodies become links and joints, <inertial> becomes explicit link inertia, and mesh geoms are assigned as link shapes and render models. A body with several collision or visual geoms gets one Hard-jointed child link per extra geom. Primitive geoms (boxes, capsules, …) are not assigned; import the MJCF in SuperDex Studio to convert them. MJCF content without a SuperDex equivalent (tendons, sites, sensors, actuator gains, …) is skipped with a logged warning.

Parameters:

path (str) – Path to the MJCF file.

Returns:

The loaded BotPrefab.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

load_bot_prefab_from_urdf_file(path: str) → BotPrefab

Load bot parameters from a URDF file.

Parses the URDF and resolves each link’s visual and collision mesh references relative to the URDF location (ROS package:// URIs are supported), storing the resolved on-disk paths in the returned prefab. Collision meshes may be any format the shape loader accepts (e.g. .stl, .obj, .ply, .off, .mochi.h5); when a collision mesh carries no baked SDF, one is generated on demand at bot creation. A free world_joint is injected at index 0. A link with several mesh <collision> or <visual> elements gets one Hard-jointed child link per extra mesh, named after the link with a _collision_k or _visual_k suffix and appended after the existing links.

Parameters:

path (str) – Path to the .urdf file.

Returns:

The loaded or built BotPrefab.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only <mesh> geometry is assigned. Primitive URDF shapes (<box>, <cylinder>, <sphere>) have no file to point at and are skipped.

Load a bot scene into a caller-provided scene from a file or archive path.

Like the prefab overload but loads and validates the BotScenePrefab through LoadBotScenePrefabFromFile so archive extraction remains transparent. The base-scene-relative root is derived analogously to the path overload (bots root with a resolved base-scene fallback), then delegates to the prefab overload. The returned BotScene owns the bots, controllers, and base-scene actors it added but leaves the caller-owned Scene intact.

Error – If an error occurs.

register_python_actuator(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register an actuator type implemented in Python. factory is called with (actor, param_args) – the link Actor, which an actuator always has, and the actuator’s params (a file path or inline JSON, empty for defaults) – and must return a Python actuator instance, which must define reset() (an empty body is fine) – the framework invokes it between episodes. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_actuator.

register_python_controller(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register a controller type implemented in Python. factory is called with the robot Actor (None if the controller was created without one) and must return a Python controller instance. The instance must define reset() (an empty body is fine); its optional configure_from_scene_entry(param_args, init_args) is also invoked by the framework. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_controller.

register_python_sensor(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register a sensor type implemented in Python. factory is called with (actor, param_args) – the link Actor, or None for an actor-less sensor, and the sensor’s params (a file path or inline JSON, empty for defaults) – and must return a Python sensor instance, which must define reset() (an empty body is fine) – the framework invokes it between episodes. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_sensor.

save_bot_scene_to_urdf_string(scene: BotScenePrefab, root_path: str, options: SceneUrdfOptions) → str

Export a bot scene to a URDF XML string, without meshes.

The URDF is rooted at a world link, the scene root. Each bot entry, base-scene articulated actor and static rigid actor hangs from it by a fixed joint named {root link}_placement, with its own links and joints unchanged below. Dynamic and soft actors, tasks and spawnable prefabs are skipped, and skins are not exported, so a skinned hand is rigid. SuperDex, unlike URDF, needs joint names to differ from link names, so a joint named like a link (e.g. “joint_01_wrist” beside “link_01_wrist”, with strip_index_prefixes) gets a _joint suffix.

Each sensor becomes a {name}_frame link at its parentFromSensor on its link (bot sensors) or on world (scene sensors). A sensor whose name another sensor shares takes its bot’s prefix, as the bot’s links do, and an unnamed sensor is named {link}_sensor_{index}, after its URDF link and its index on that link. A camera’s parentFromSensor is its optical frame (Z forward, X right, Y down): it gets a {name}_optical_frame link there, and {name}_frame follows ROS REP-103 (X forward, Z up). Intrinsics are not exported.

No <visual> or <collision> elements are written. SuperDex Studio’s scene_to_urdf exports the meshes too, as STL.

Parameters:

  • scene (BotScenePrefab) – Path-resolved scene, as returned by load_bot_scene_prefab_from_file().

  • root_path (str) – Root directory for the base scene’s relative paths (see GetBotSceneBaseRoot).

  • options (SceneUrdfOptions) – Export options.

Returns:

The URDF XML.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.
